summary.title: LongStraw: Long-Context RL Beyond 2M Tokens under a Fixed GPU Budget

setting_and_object.category: Algorithm / System (execution stack for long-context RL post-training)

details: In GRPO, one multi-million-token prompt must condition old-policy, reference, and G policy responses; conventional autograd keeps the prompt graph plus all response graphs live, so million-token RL post-training does not fit a fixed accelerator inventory (attention-kernel efficiency, LoRA/QLoRA, or sparsity alone do not fix it).
Complementary to scale-out sequence-parallel systems: the question is how much GRPO-shaped execution fits without adding devices.

LongStraw: an objective- and architecture-aware transaction that evaluates the shared prompt once with autograd disabled, retains only the architecture-required conditional state (recurrent state / KV pages, or MLA latent + DSA indexer-key pages) on right-sized, explicitly owned physical pages, restores that read-only state for every group member, scores old/reference branches without a graph, then replays one response suffix at a time under autograd and accumulates gradients before a single distributed gradient finalization and optimizer step.

Formally it computes only the first term of the gradient (stop-grad on the prompt state), bounding live-graph memory by the response suffix rather than by prompt length or group size; group cardinality becomes a scheduling/time axis.

Same transaction contract is specialized per architecture in retained state, replay operator, and collectives (page-owner KV pages plus cross-rank LSE/output merge for a hybrid recurrent/attention stack; CPU-resident layer-staged MLA/DSA pages, global cross-CP sparse selection, and EP token dispatch for an MLA/DSA + MoE stack).

Qwen3.6-27B snapshot: 64 decoder layers, hidden 5,120, 48 GDN (linear-attention) + 16 full GQA layers (24 Q heads, 4 KV heads, head dim 256), dense SwiGLU FFN width 17,408; NF4 QLoRA rank 16, alpha 32, 116,727,808 trainable parameters.

GLM-5.2 snapshot: 78 layers, hidden 6,144, 64 MLA query heads, Q/KV latent 2,048/512, DSA indexer 32 heads x 128 selecting top-2,048 positions, 21 index-computing layers + 57 IndexShare consumers, first 3 dense FFNs then 75 MoE layers (256 routed experts, top-8, one shared expert, expert width 2,048); LoRA rank 8 over attention/dense/routed/shared-expert projections and output head, base weights, norms, router, and DSA indexer frozen.
Runs inside the MinT training plane with Ray-resident Megatron workers; Qwen prototype reuses OOMB chunkoptim cache/paged-attention kernels as components.

Qwen: fixed 8 H20 GPUs, CP8, page size 64, block-cyclic page ownership (p mod 8), compact GPU pages, lazily allocated and pruned detached-prefix gradient pages; prompt captured in 510 chunks of 4,096; response split into four 2,048-token blocks replayed in reverse with whole-layer checkpointing and 512-token backward MLP microblocks.

GLM: fixed 32 H20 GPUs, training TP1/CP32/EP32/ETP1/PP1 with Megatron zigzag CP pages (rank r owns chunks r and 63-r; 1,024 pages = 65,536 tokens per rank), CPU-resident MLA (72 MiB/layer) and DSA index-key (16 MiB/layer) pages totaling 5.8125 GiB per rank, one-layer GPU staging, reentrant whole-decoder-layer checkpointing, shared RoPE cache.

GLM online phase time-shares the same 32 GPUs: Megatron actor released, Tinker-managed multi-node vLLM sampler at TP8/PP4 loads a vLLM-compatible projection of the rank-8 policy LoRA (content hash checked across handoff), then Megatron restored.

Qwen 2M receipt: 2,088,960 prompt + 8,192 response-input tokens = 2,097,152 positions (8x the 262,144 native setting), G=2 and G=8, synthetic random tokens, deterministic rewards, old/reference scores from the same runner, beta=0, unclipped live ratio term.

Qwen 4.25M receipt: 4,448,256 prompt + 8,192 response = 4,456,448 positions, G=8, one resident prefix reused across eight accumulate-and-step cycles (64 member replays); separate 1M probe on real DAPO text compares recaptured vs resident prefix.

GLM exact-2M receipt: one real DAPO-MATH example with exactly 2,097,152 prompt tokens, two five-token vLLM completions (four scored log-probs each), ground-truth rewards [-1,+1], G=2, epsilon=0.2, beta=0 (old snapshot serves as reference); rollout and training share an opt-in YaRN factor 2.000015 with max_position_embeddings=2097168 over the 1,048,576 native context.

concrete_detailed_setting.aspect: Staged diagnostics, validation levels, and ablations
details: Eight-stage GLM progression: full-graph OOM localization at 2M, prefix-only capture sweep (128K/256K/512K/1M/2.097M), single-layer differentiable replay, all-layer 32K/64K integration (IndexShare lifetime, view/in-place fixes, checkpoint boundary), CP32/EP32 + CPU pages, G=1 control, predecessor grouped G=2 run, and the final exact-2M online transaction.

Three explicit validation levels reported separately: execution capacity (per-rank logs/traces), response-operator fidelity (global CP8 LSE merge with BF16 numerator reduction; global cross-CP32 DSA candidate/value exchange), and distributed-update consistency (finalize_model_grads before one step for GLM; Qwen's page-owner dK/dV to replicated adapters kept as a separate audit).

Ablations/variants: batched old/reference scoring, attention-only vs whole-layer checkpointing, logical-view vs right-sized physical pages, detached-prefix gradient-page pruning, and train-block capacity brackets (pass at 4,538,368, OOM at 4,542,464).

key_findings.finding: Serializing response replay after one no-grad prompt capture makes GRPO group size a time axis rather than a memory axis at multi-million-token context.
key_findings.evidence: On 8 H20 GPUs at 2,097,152 positions, going from G=2 to G=8 raised peak allocated memory only from 97.503 to 97.711 GB (+0.208 GB, +0.213%) while wall time rose from 5,198.780 to 6,785.225 s; post-prefix cost per member was 271.278 vs 266.476 s and mean wall time per response fell from 2,599.390 to 848.153 s as the ~4,655 s prefix was amortized.

key_findings.finding: The complete exact-2M online GRPO transaction (rollout, reward, global sparse attention, response backwards, distributed gradient finalization, optimizer step) fits on 32 fixed GPUs by time-multiplexing rollout and training topologies.
key_findings.evidence: For GLM-5.2, a Tinker-managed vLLM sampler at TP8/PP4 processed a real 2,097,152-token DAPO-MATH prompt, produced two completions with rewards [-1,+1] (activating one lower and one upper clip at epsilon=0.2), then the same 32 GPUs ran Megatron TP1/CP32/EP32 with global cross-CP DSA, two 78-layer response backwards, finalize_model_grads, and one optimizer step on every rank; 64 trace files with 25,536 events (3,648 global-position DSA and 1,344 fused global-indexer events) contain no non-finite values or errors.

key_findings.finding: Physical allocator ownership, not logical sharding, determines whether context-parallel pages actually reduce memory.
key_findings.evidence: An early Qwen 2M prefix capture whose page shards were views into 4,096-token parent chunks stopped after 352 of 510 chunks at ~136.068 GB; copying each owned slice into a right-sized allocation completed all 510 chunks at a 58.655 GB prefix peak.

key_findings.finding: Under the same eight-GPU budget the design reaches 4.25M positions and supports repeated updates by keeping the prefix resident, though resident reuse drifts from exact recapture after a few steps.
key_findings.evidence: At 4,456,448 positions, eight consecutive G=8 accumulate-and-step cycles (64 member replays) completed with every rank recording an applied optimizer step at 83.894 GB per rank; one prefix capture cost 17,729.8 s versus ~4,051 s per post-prefix cycle (an estimated 34.5 h of avoided prefill). A 1M real-DAPO probe showed recaptured-vs-resident GRPO loss differing by +0.1236% and +0.0378% at steps 1-2 but -22.81% and -9.33% at steps 4 and 8 (mean absolute log-prob differences 0.0137/0.0250 vs 3.136/3.774).

key_findings.finding: Architectural sparsity (DSA, MoE) transfers rather than removes the memory cost, so only prompt-graph lifetime plus whole-layer checkpointing brings the MoE stack within budget.
key_findings.evidence: Full-sequence 2M GLM attempts OOMed in a chain: FP32 DSA score scratch [8192, 2,097,152] ~64 GiB, then expert-LoRA scale/add 7.80 GiB and an FC2 matmul 11.70 GiB, then expert-output concatenation requesting 19.37 GiB; at a 65,536-token CP shard, top-8 routing alone yields a 6 GiB BF16 [524,288 x 6,144] buffer. Attention-only checkpointing left router/dispatch/expert/LoRA tensors live, requiring complete-decoder-layer checkpointing. A batched old/reference-scoring variant saved only 0.7% post-prefix time at 4.25M while raising peak memory from 83.894 to 135.128 GB.
